title: Void Ending in a Conjunction with Sun
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The conjunction is the closest bond the Moon makes: at it, her strength takes on the nature of the planet she has joined, and the doctrine of the fifth quality treats her meeting with the Sun as the strongest of all her figures. A course that closes on a conjunction ends in union rather than separation, the Moon's virtue soaked through with the planet's own nature.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a conjunction with Sun, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his light and his generative heat. Picatrix calls the Sun the light of the world and the axis on which the universe turns; generative power flows from him, the heart is his seat in the body, gold is his metal, and the ruby and the jacinth his stones. His benevolence fits great royal achievements and kings. The whole lunar doctrine hangs on him, for in the text's accounting the stars and the Moon together sustain all vegetation and every composite body.
